Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

kill verb

also killing, slay, put to death, kill time, you’re killing me!

classical

Caes. BG 1.12.5: L. Cassium cōnsulem interfēcerat

interficiō, interficere, interfēcī, interfectum

verb, third conjugation

The general word of prose (Lewis & Short, with the synonyms necō, occīdō, trucīdō).

Examples

  • parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum

    a small viper kills a huge bull with its biteOv. Rem. 421

  • et cum ille, quī quaesierat, dīxisset: «quid faenerārī?», tum Catō: «quid hominem,» inquit, «occīdere?»

    and when the man who had asked said, “What about lending money at interest?”, Cato replied, “What about killing a man?”Cic. Off. 2.89

  • lassitūdinem hercle verba tua mihi addunt, ēnicās

    your words are wearing me out, really — you’re killing mePlaut. Merc. 157

Other words

  • occīdō, occīdere, occīdī, occīsum — strike down, kill

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.89: quid hominem occīdere?; Traupman 336

    From caedō, with a long ī; not occidō, fall, set (of the sun).

  • necō, necāre, necāvī, necātum — kill, put to death (usually without a weapon)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. Rem. 421: parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum; Phaedr. 5.3.10: optem necāre; Traupman 336

    Lewis & Short: “usually without a weapon, by poison, hunger, etc.”; Festus (in Paulus’ epitome) distinguishes it from occīdere, killing by a blow.

  • trucīdō, trucīdāre, trucīdāvī, trucīdātum — slaughter, butcher

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 7: cīvēs Rōmānōs necandōs trucīdandōsque cūrāvit (Lewis & Short)

  • ēnecō (ēnicō), ēnecāre, ēnecuī, ēnectum — kill off; wear out: ēnicās, you’re killing me!

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 157: verba tua mihi addunt, ēnicās; Traupman 336: mē ēnicās!

    (vōx cōmica in the sense “wear out”: Plaut.)

    In comedy, the complaint of someone pestered past bearing.

See also die, wound, attack.

SourcesLewis & Short: interficio · Lewis & Short: occido · Lewis & Short: neco · Lewis & Short: trucido · Lewis & Short: eneco
